title: Lesson 3: Core Building Blocks: Objects, Fields, Relationships, Record Types, and Formula vs Roll-Up
description: The architect's canvas: standard and custom objects, field types, lookup vs master-detail relationships, record types for process variation, and when to compute with a formula field vs a roll-up summary.

questions.question: What does a master-detail relationship provide that a lookup relationship does not?
options: Inherited detail security and roll-up summaries on the master.
An independent security model and a visible Owner field on the detail.
A way to relate two objects that otherwise have no relationship.
The ability to store one record inside two different objects.
questions.explanation: Master-detail makes the master own the detail, so the detail inherits the master's security and ownership and roll-ups become available; a lookup supports neither.

questions.question: When should an architect choose a roll-up summary instead of a formula field?
options: When a value can be computed from fields within a single record.
When the value must update in real time on each record view.
When a value aggregates many child records onto the master.
When the value must be shown on a report or a list view.
questions.explanation: Roll-up summaries aggregate COUNT, SUM, MIN, or MAX from related child records onto a master, which a formula cannot do.

questions.question: What are record types intended to model?
options: Genuinely different fields and visibility between two business units.
Different processes, picklists, and layouts within one data shape.
Separate objects that share a single field set and sharing model.
A way to control which existing records a user is allowed to view.
questions.explanation: Record types vary the process, picklist values, and layout for one object; they share one field set and sharing model and do not gate record visibility.
